issue.title: Discard the task state values for a task instance when it is cleared

labels.name: area:UI
labels.description: Related to UI/UX. For Frontend Developers.

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body: --- ##### Was generative AI tooling used to co-author this PR? - [ ] Yes (please specify the tool below) ## Summary Clearing a task instance now discards its `task_state_store` entries, so the next attempt starts over instead of resuming from a checkpoint or reconnecting to an external job recorded by the attempt that was cleared. Clearing a task instance now discards its `task_state_store` entries, so the next attempt starts over. Retries are unaffected and still resume. ## Why A retry and a clear were treated identically. Both kept the task's state, both resumed. But they mean different things. A retry happens because infrastructure failed. Nothing about the work changed, so carrying on from the checkpoint is exactly right, and that is what crash recovery is for. A clear happens because a human intervened, and the usual reason a human clears a task is that something *did* change: the code, the upstream data, a connection, a config value. So the behaviour was tuned for the case where nothing changed, and then applied to the case where something had. What that cost in practice: **Fixing a bug and clearing left the bug's output in place.** A task gets through files 1 to 6, hits bad data on the 7th, you fix the transform and clear. It resumed at 7. Files 1 to 6 still held output from the code you had just fixed, now silently mixed with the corrected work. The task went green, and nothing anywhere said otherwise. **Clearing a succeeded durable task did nothing at all.** The operator read back the stored job id, saw the external job had already finished, and returned the stored result in a couple of seconds. This needs no unusual configuration, and there is no reading of "clear" under which doing nothing is what the user asked for. The two failure modes are asymmetric, which is what decides the default rather than just moving the problem elsewhere. Discarding when you wanted to resume costs repeated work you can watch happen. Resuming when you wanted a fresh start produces wrong output you cannot see. ## What changed - `keep_task_state` on `ClearTaskInstancesBody`, defaulting to `false` - The discard runs in `post_clear_task_instances`, inside the existing `if not dry_run:` block and after `clear_task_instances` succeeds, so a preview discards nothing and a failed clear cannot take the task state with it - `_clear_task_state_store_on_success` refactored into a shared `discard_task_state_store` helper: two callers, two gates, one implementation - A "Keep task state and resume" checkbox in both clear dialogs, unchecked by default, next to the existing "Prevent rerun if task is running" - Concept docs rewritten. The section previously asserted the opposite, under the heading "Clearing a task is treated the same as a retry" ## When to tick the box Two situations, both documented. **Nothing changed and you only want the task to carry on.** Retries normally cover this, so you reach it when retries are exhausted. **An external job is still running.** Most operators cancel theirs in `on_kill`, so clearing a *running* task leaves nothing to reconnect to. But clearing a *failed* task never runs `on_kill`, so a job that outlived its worker is still going, and discarding the stored id submits a second one. Same for operators configured to leave the job alive, such as `KubernetesPodOperator` with `on_kill_action="keep_pod"`. ## Compatibility This changes behaviour introduced in 3.3 and released in 3.3.1. Anyone relying on clear-to-resume needs `keep_task_state=true`. A single default rather than per-operator behaviour is acceptable precisely because the user keeps an override: if Airflow decided silently per operator, a wrong guess would be unrecoverable, whereas a wrong default is one checkbox. ## Tests Trying to run a dag like this: ``` from __future__ import annotations import logging from datetime import datetime from airflow.sdk import DAG, NEVER_EXPIRE, Variable, task log = logging.getLogger("airflow.task") ROWS = ["100", "200", "N/A", "400", "500"] with DAG( dag_id="clear_after_fix", schedule=None, start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1), catchup=False, tags=["task-state-store"], doc_md=__doc__, ): @task(retries=0) def transform_amounts(**context): store = context["task_state_store"] handle_missing = Variable.get("handle_missing", default="false") == "true" done = set(store.get("done", default=[])) if done: log.info("Resuming, %d of %d rows already done", len(done), len(ROWS)) else: log.info("Starting fresh, %d rows to transform", len(ROWS)) total = 0 for row in ROWS: if row in done: log.info(" %-5s skipped, already done", row) continue if row == "N/A" and not handle_missing: raise ValueError(f"cannot transform {row!r}: fix the transform and clear this task") total += 0 if row == "N/A" else int(row) done.add(row) store.set("done", sorted(done), retention=NEVER_EXPIRE) log.info(" %-5s transformed", row) log.info("Done. %d rows, total %d", len(done), total) return total transform_amounts() ``` This dag showcases some data transformation and mimics a case where bad data came in as `N/A` controlled by a variable value. So showing it: First run: Task state store contains this: Set the variable rightly now: `airflow variables set handle_missing true` Clear with the default: Next run: State store: Now if I cleared by overriding the checkbox for another try (ie: keeping task state): Observe the logs: ### More testing Tried same test as above from clear from TI page as bulk Clearing with airflowctl: ```shell amoghrajesh.desai  …/airflow   task-state-clear-on-clear $!?   orbstack  ♥ 12:28  airflowctl tasks clear --help Usage: airflowctl tasks clear [-h] [--api-token API_TOKEN] [--dag-run-id DAG_RUN_ID] [--dry-run | --no-dry-run] [--end-date END_DATE] [-e ENV] [--include-downstream | --no-include-downstream] [--include-future | --no-include-future] [--include-past | --no-include-past] [--include-upstream | --no-include-upstream] [--keep-task-state | --no-keep-task-state] [--note NOTE] [--only-failed | --no-only-failed] [--only-running | --no-only-running] [--prevent-running-task | --no-prevent-running-task] [--reset-dag-runs | --no-reset-dag-runs] [--run-on-latest-version | --no-run-on-latest-version] [--start-date START_DATE] [--task-ids TASK_IDS] [--output (table, json, yaml, plain)] dag_id Clear task instances of a Dag by its ID Positional Arguments: dag_id dag_id for clear operation in TasksOperations Options: -h, --help show this help message and exit --api-token API_TOKEN The token to use for authentication --dag-run-id DAG_RUN_ID dag_run_id for clear_task_instances operation --dry-run, --no-dry-run dry_run for clear_task_instances operation --end-date END_DATE end_date for clear_task_instances operation -e, --env ENV The environment to run the command in --include-downstream, --no-include-downstream include_downstream for clear_task_instances operation --include-future, --no-include-future include_future for clear_task_instances operation --include-past, --no-include-past include_past for clear_task_instances operation --include-upstream, --no-include-upstream include_upstream for clear_task_instances operation --keep-task-state, --no-keep-task-state keep_task_state for clear_task_instances operation --note NOTE note for clear_task_instances operation --only-failed, --no-only-failed only_failed for clear_task_instances operation --only-running, --no-only-running only_running for clear_task_instances operation --prevent-running-task, --no-prevent-running-task prevent_running_task for clear_task_instances operation --reset-dag-runs, --no-reset-dag-runs reset_dag_runs for clear_task_instances operation --run-on-latest-version, --no-run-on-latest-version run_on_latest_version for clear_task_instances operation --start-date START_DATE start_date for clear_task_instances operation --task-ids TASK_IDS task_ids for clear_task_instances operation --output, -o (table, json, yaml, plain) Output format. Allowed values: json, yaml, plain, table (default: json) ``` Ran this: ```shell [Breeze:3.11.15] root@3c493b69b8c3:/opt/airflow$ airflowctl dags tasks clear_after_fix --run-id manual__2026-09-09T07:30:58.621788+00:00 Please enter password for encrypted keyring: Dag: clear_after_fix Dag runs to clear: 1 - manual__2026-09-09T07:30:58.621788+00:00 (logical date: 2026-09-09T07:30:57+00:00, partition date: -) Clear task instances for these Dag runs? [y/N] y Cleared 1 task instance(s) across 1 Dag run(s) ``` --- * Read the **[Pull Request Guidelines](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/contributing-docs/05_pull_requests.rst#pull-request-guidelines)** for more information. body:
Reproduced on current main: clearing a Dag run leaves its `task_state_store` checkpoint behind. The new regression fails before the fix, while the existing clear test passes.

A local fix moves deletion into `clear_task_instances()` and threads the preservation option through single/bulk Dag-run clear and both core CLI clear commands. Tests cover default deletion, explicit preservation, dry-run, untouched scopes, and downstream clearing. The related PostgreSQL suite passed with 1,057 tests; an additional Dag/clear suite passed with 335 tests (the suites overlap).

The patch and PR description are prepared locally; a PR has not been opened yet.

issue.title: Discard task checkpoints consistently when clearing tasks

labels.name: area:UI
labels.description: Related to UI/UX. For Frontend Developers.

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Clearing a Dag run or using the core CLI currently leaves task-state checkpoints behind, even though clearing through the task-instance endpoint discards them. Move deletion into `clear_task_instances()` so those paths and downstream clearing share the same default.

Add `keep_task_state` to single and bulk Dag-run clear requests, and `--keep-task-state` to `airflow dags clear` and `airflow tasks clear`. Preserve dry-run behavior and untouched scopes. Update resumable-task documentation and regenerate OpenAPI and its clients.

Expose “Keep task state and resume” in both single and bulk Dag-run clear dialogs, using the existing saved default. Both dialogs explicitly send the selected value on confirmation.

Validation on PostgreSQL with Breeze/Python 3.12:

- Captured the default-clear regression failing before the fix; explicit preservation options also failed with HTTP 422.
- Related API, CLI, and task-instance suite: 1,057 passed, four skipped.
- Additional Dag/model and clear-path suite: 335 passed, including downstream checkpoint deletion.
- UI request tests: nine passed, including default false, explicit true, saved defaults, and overriding a saved true default. UI lint, TypeScript checking, and the production build passed.
- Changed-file pre-commit checks and applicable manual checks passed. The OpenAPI hook hard-codes Python 3.10; its generator was run successfully in the available Python 3.12 Breeze environment instead.
- Repository-wide checks remain incomplete: unrelated provider generators attempted separate Python 3.10 image builds, which were stopped. No repository-wide pass is claimed.

The pre-existing limitation for custom state-store backends is unchanged.

closes: #72929

issue.title: Reset a mapped task's state store when its expansion is recomputed

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
Opened fresh from #73375, which was closed under the new open-PR-limit policy and then failed to reopen (both `gh pr reopen` and the UI button errored with a generic "Could not open the pull request") — following @potiuk's guidance on Slack to push/open fresh from the branch when reopening doesn't work.

The task state store is keyed by the positional `map_index`, and it survives a clear on purpose, so a cleared task resumes from its last checkpoint. As #72725 shows, that stops being safe for a mapped task once the list it expands over changes. Clear the upstream task with its downstream, the upstream returns `["z", "a", "b", "c"]` instead of `["a", "b", "c"]`, and map index 0 now processes `z` while reading the checkpoint written for `a`. The run still succeeds.

The list can only change when the task that produces it runs again. So this deletes a mapped task's state store rows, for every map index in that run, when a task it expands over is cleared, and leaves them alone otherwise:

| What is cleared | Mapped task's state |
| --- | --- |
| The task it expands over, alone or with downstream | deleted, all map indices |
| The whole Dag run | deleted |
| Only the mapped task | kept, it resumes as documented |
| Unmapped tasks, and mapped tasks over a literal list | kept |

Tasks inside a mapped task group are handled the same way, using the group's expansion input. The check runs in `clear_task_instances`, which both `dag.clear()` and the clear endpoints go through. It resolves the Dag on the same version the cleared task instances will run on, and logs how many rows it deleted.

This differs from #72788, which deletes a task's rows on every clear. That also covers this case, but it removes the resume-after-clear behaviour that `resumable-tasks.rst` documents for unmapped tasks and for mapped tasks whose input is unchanged. The trade-off here is that a mapped task whose upstream is cleared starts over even if the upstream happens to return the same list again. Comparing the lists would need the old values, which are not stored.

The docs now say this in the "Mapped tasks" section of `task-state-store.rst` and in the clearing note in `resumable-tasks.rst`. The task state store is not in a release yet (3.3.2 does not have it), so I did not add a newsfragment.

Tests:

- New tests in `test_cleartasks.py` cover the cases in the table, a mapped task group, a second run of the same Dag that is left alone, and `dag.clear()` with downstream. With the new call skipped, every case that expects rows to be deleted fails. The "only the mapped task" case passes either way, which is the point of that case.
- An end-to-end check that I did not commit: each map index wrote its item through the Execution API task state store endpoint, then the task run was cleared, then the new task instances read their checkpoints back. After clearing the upstream they got `{0: 404, 1: 404, 2: 404}` with this change, and `{0: "a", 1: "b", 2: "c"}` without it, which is the stale state from the issue. After clearing only the mapped task they got `{0: "a", 1: "b", 2: "c"}` both ways.
- `test_cleartasks.py` passes on SQLite and on Postgres 16 (47 passed). The execution API and public API task state store tests pass, as do the clear tests in the public task instances API and `test_dag.py`. prek passes, including mypy for airflow-core.

closes: #72725

issue.title: Add durable reconnect option to EmrServerlessStartJobOperator

repository.name: airflow
repository.description: Apache Airflow - A platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows

issue.body:
This adds a `durable` option to `EmrServerlessStartJobOperator` that persists the submitted job run id to task state (Airflow 3.3+) and, on a retry or a manual clear/rerun, reconnects to the still-running (or already-succeeded) job run instead of submitting a duplicate.

## Motivation

On a clear/retry today, a deferrable EMR Serverless task re-runs `execute()` and starts a brand-new job run, so the original hourly-billed Spark job is duplicated. `GlueJobOperator` already avoids this via its `durable` option; EMR Serverless had no equivalent, so the two Spark-submitting operators behaved differently on the same user action. This brings them into line.

## Behaviour

- `durable=True` → on a retry or clear, reconnect to the still-running job (no duplicate, no re-bill). If the prior run already **succeeded**, return it without re-running. If the prior run is terminal-failed, submit fresh.
- `durable=False` (default) → unchanged behaviour.

Has no effect on Airflow < 3.3 (task state unavailable), where it degrades to a fresh submit.

**Clearing on Airflow 3.4+.** Since #72100, clearing a task discards its task state unless `keep_task_state` is set ("retries resume, clearing starts over"). So `durable` reconnects on retries and on clears that keep task state; a plain clear submits a new run, and a task that had already succeeded runs again. With `cancel_on_kill` off (the `durable` default in deferrable mode) the old run keeps going after a plain clear, so set `cancel_on_kill=True` to stop it. The CLI `airflow tasks clear` and clearing a whole Dag run still keep task state (#72929). `GlueJobOperator`'s deferrable path differs here because it finds the previous run by a task-UUID scan rather than task state, so it reattaches on any clear.

### `durable` with `cancel_on_kill` in deferrable mode

In deferrable mode the trigger's `on_kill` cancels the job on any user action, and it cannot tell a clear (which re-runs the task) from mark failed/success. On clear the worker re-executes `execute()` **before** the triggerer calls `on_kill` (measured ~0.5s earlier on live AWS), so a durable retry would reconnect to a run `on_kill` then cancels, failing the task. The two options are resolved the same way as `GlueJobOperator`'s `durable` with `stop_job_run_on_kill` (#73702):

- `durable=True` with `cancel_on_kill` **unset** turns `cancel_on_kill` off (deferrable, Airflow 3.3+ only), so reconnect-on-clear is what `durable` gives by default. Marking the task failed then leaves the job running, as with Glue's default.
- `durable=True` with `cancel_on_kill=True` **set explicitly**: a retried try does not reconnect. It cancels the stored run if it is still active and submits a fresh one. Unlike Glue, it does not wait for the cancellation to finish, since EMR Serverless has no per-job concurrency limit.
- Below Airflow 3.3 `durable` does nothing, so `cancel_on_kill` keeps its default there.
- Synchronous mode is unchanged: `cancel_on_kill` does not apply (the operator's own `on_kill` always cancels).

A stored run that already succeeded is returned before the application is started, so clearing a finished task does not wake up a stopped application.

## Validated on live AWS

EMR Serverless (ap-northeast-2), standalone Airflow on `main` (3.4.0.dev, before #72100) plus this branch, Spark sleep job:

| config | behaviour after clear | result |
|---|---|---|
| `durable=True` (cancel_on_kill forced off) | reconnect to the running run | PASS — 1 run |
| `durable=True`, cleared after success | reconnect to the succeeded run, no re-run | PASS — 1 run |
| `durable=False` (baseline) | new run submitted, old not reconnected | reproduces the pre-existing gap — 2 runs |
| `durable=True` + `cancel_on_kill=True` (deferrable) | cancel the previous run, submit fresh | not yet re-validated after this change |

## Implementation notes / reviewer questions

1. **Default value.** Kept `durable=False`; `GlueJobOperator` defaults `durable=True` on 3.3+. Happy to raise the default if preferred.
2. **Why not `ResumableJobMixin`.** `execute_resumable` blocks on `poll_until_complete`, so it is synchronous-only and cannot serve the deferrable path — the case that matters for EMR Serverless. The reconnect is implemented directly in `execute()` (covering both the synchronous and deferrable paths), but it is a faithful port of the mixin: the same decision tree (active → reconnect / succeeded → skip / terminal → resubmit) and the same persist timing with `retention` omitted (30-day `[state_store] default_retention_days`, matching the mixin). Related: #71485.

## Testing

- New unit tests: reconnect-to-active, reconnect-to-succeeded (returns before the application start), resubmit-on-terminal, fresh-submit persistence, no-store fallback, `durable=False` no-op, deferrable reconnect, deferrable `durable` + explicit `cancel_on_kill=True` cancelling the previous run and submitting fresh (including when the cancel is rejected and when the run already succeeded), and the `cancel_on_kill` default with `durable` on and below Airflow 3.3.
- `test_emr_serverless.py` + EMR trigger suites pass locally, except two untouched `TestEmrServerlessStopOperator` tests that error on a local venv import (`airflow_shared` in the `caplog` fixture) and pass in another checkout.
- Live-AWS matrix above (the explicit `cancel_on_kill=True` row still to be re-run).
- `prek` pre-commit hooks and provider `mypy` (`breeze run mypy`) on the changed files pass.

issue.title: Fix asset outlets and load revision, add durable load and push, use ASF headers
issue.body:
Fixes from my review of the MVP for the provider proposal (https://github.com/huggingface/datasets/discussions/8882). Each one is a separate commit, so you can drop any you disagree with.

- **License headers.** `__init__.py` had a "Copyright 2020 The HuggingFace Datasets Authors and the TensorFlow Datasets Authors" notice above the ASF header, and the other Python files had no header. Code proposed for Airflow needs the ASF header on every source file. If any of this was copied from `datasets`, tell me and we'll keep the attribution in a NOTICE file instead.
- **Install instructions.** The README and the MRPC example installed `hf-datasets-airflow-provider`. That isn't the package this repo builds, and it isn't on PyPI. Both now install from git. Please don't publish `apache-airflow-providers-huggingface` to PyPI from here, because that prefix is reserved for releases made by the ASF.
- **`PushToHubOperator` outlets.** Passing `outlets=` raised `TypeError: got multiple values for keyword argument 'outlets'`. The user's outlets are now kept, and the Hub asset is added to them.
- **`PushToHubOperator` with a templated `repo_id`.** The asset was built from the unrendered value, so `repo_id="{{ params.repo }}"` emitted an event for `huggingface://datasets/{{ params.repo }}`. Downstream Dags schedule on a fixed asset, so `repo_id` is no longer a template field, and a Jinja expression in it fails when the Dag is parsed.
- **Revision recorded on load.** `LoadDatasetOperator` loaded the requested revision first and looked up the commit sha afterwards. With `main`, a commit landing in between made XCom record a revision that wasn't the one loaded. It now resolves the ref to a commit, loads that commit, and records it. `datasets` does the same internally.

- **Durable load and push on Airflow 3.3+.** This answers the cache and retry question from the discussion using Airflow's task state store. A new `durable` parameter, on by default, makes `LoadDatasetOperator` keep the commit it pinned, so retries load that commit even after `main` moves. `PushToHubOperator` keeps the commit sha after a successful upload, so a retry after a later failure (such as the card upload) emits the asset event without uploading again. On Airflow below 3.3 there's no task state store, and nothing changes.

One behaviour change: if a Hub dataset's revision can't be resolved, the task now fails instead of logging a warning. An existing local directory is never looked up on the Hub.

There is one gotcha with durable push. Clearing a single task from the UI or API discards its task state, but clearing a whole Dag run keeps it (apache/airflow#72929). So after fixing a transform and clearing the run, a stored commit would wrongly skip the new upload. To prevent that, every operator now records the Datasets fingerprint of what it saved, and the push only reuses a stored commit when the input's fingerprint matches. The fingerprint is deterministic for the same data and transform, and it changes when either changes. An input passed as a plain URI has no fingerprint, so it is always pushed.

The other design points from the review aren't in this PR, because those are your call: object storage for handing data between tasks, `hf://` asset URIs, callable transforms, and narrowing the first release to load, map and push.
